pure-announcement.rationale: It is third-party explainer coverage of the Agent Skills technique, not a vendor launch, release note, or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: Its central idea — a SKILL.md folder standard with three-tier progressive disclosure, portable across compliant agents — is exactly what the existing agent-skills-format concept already states, leaving only ephemeral extras (adoption timeline, directory paths, marketplace counts) that add no new conceptual content.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The core claims cite checkable primary sources (agentskills.io spec, Anthropic docs, the anthropics/skills and openai/skills repos), even if some adoption figures are journalistic.

durability.rationale: Much of its bulk is adoption-count and catalog material — 32 tools, tens of thousands of marketplace listings, per-tool directory paths, a quarter-stamped 'Skills 2.0' timeline — which the article itself warns may change, while the durable architecture is already captured elsewhere.

actionability.rationale: The authoring walkthrough (description field does the triggering, keep the body under ~5k tokens, split references into secondary files) and the three security vetting rules give a reader concrete, tool-spanning practice to apply.

atomicity.rationale: It bundles a standard explainer, an adoption timeline, a Skills-vs-MCP-vs-subagents comparison, a directory map, an authoring guide, marketplace analysis, and security guidance — several separable strands under one umbrella.
